column2: They had three lifeboats, sledges, some tents and food for a few weeks.
Shackleton told every man to keep only two pounds of personal things. Everything else stayed on the ice.
He went first. He threw away gold coins, and a Bible after tearing out a few pages.
Hurley had to smash many of his glass negatives. He kept around a hundred and fifty. Those are the photos we have today.
They tried to drag the boats across the ice towards land. Each boat weighed about a tonne.
After three hours of hauling, they had moved about one mile. Shackleton stopped the march.
They set up camp on a big floe and named it Ocean Camp.
On the twenty-first of November 1915, the men watched Endurance finally sink. Shackleton said only: She's gone, boys.
In late December they tried another march, and gave up again after a week. The new camp was called Patience Camp.
Food was rationed hard. They hunted seals and penguins, and later had to put down the sledge dogs.
One day a sea leopard chased a man across the ice. Frank Wild shot it. It fed the camp for days.
To drink, they packed snow into tins and held them against their bodies to melt it.
And Shackleton made sure every man had a job. He knew that the real danger was not only cold. It was despair.
